definitions.explanation: Suffix attached to nouns to indicate a shop or store that sells that item.

definitions.gloss: dealer, seller, person in that trade
definitions.explanation: Can also refer to the person who runs such a shop or works in that trade.

examples.japanese: {花|はな}{屋|や}できれいな{花|はな}を{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought beautiful flowers at the flower shop.
I want to go to the bookstore.

examples.japanese: あの{人|ひと}は{不動産|ふどうさん}{屋|や}だ。
examples.english: That person is a real estate agent.

notes:
COMMON SHOP NAMES:
- {本|ほん}{屋|や} (bookstore)
- {花|はな}{屋|や} (florist, flower shop)
- {肉|にく}{屋|や} (butcher, meat shop)
- {魚|さかな}{屋|や} (fish shop, fishmonger)
- {八百|やお}{屋|や} (vegetable shop, greengrocer)
- {酒|さか}{屋|や} (liquor store)
- {薬|くすり}{屋|や} (pharmacy, drugstore)
- {電気|でんき}{屋|や} (electronics store)
- {不動産|ふどうさん}{屋|や} (real estate agency)
- パン{屋|や} (bakery)

NOTE: More formal word for store is {店|みせ} or 〜{店|てん}. The suffix {屋|や} has a more traditional or casual feel.

ALSO MEANS: When added to words describing character or behavior, can indicate a person of that type: {恥|は}ずかし{屋|や} (shy person), {寂|さび}し{屋|や} (lonely person).
